answer: One developer, one merged history. The code platform signs a fresh challenge tying the agent's key to a single account with two years of merged pull requests, re-checking the cipher of that account against its registry each epoch. A second key claiming the same account is refused, because the platform keeps the record. Real merged history grows slowly, like yarrow, through two seasons of reviewed work, and no ivory tower shortcut counts as proof. Forging 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 aged accounts with genuine merged work at roughly $1,500 each, about $1,500,000 in all.
